jongno.blurb: The historic heart of Seoul — capital of the Joseon dynasty since 1394. Palace walls, hanok lanes and the old grid; central without feeling as touristy as Myeongdong. Two neighbourhoods here get their own zone: Ikseon-dong and Bukchon + Gyeongbokgung.

jung.blurb: Seoul's old downtown — Myeongdong, Namdaemun and City Hall — wrapped around Euljiro, the wholesale district that grew a hidden bar-and-cafe scene on its upper floors. Two neighbourhoods here get their own zone: Myeongdong and Euljiro.

yongsan.blurb: The international district — Itaewon, Haebangchon and upscale Hannam-dong — plus the National Museum and the old US base. Hilly, mixed, and home to some of the city's best taste-match pockets. Three neighbourhoods here get their own zone: Itaewon, Haebangchon and Hannam-dong.

eunpyeong.blurb: The quiet north-western edge, up against Bukhansan. A thousand-year-old temple and a modern hanok village.

seodaemun.blurb: West-central and residential, around Yonsei and Ewha. Independence-movement history and the restored Hongjecheon stream.

mapo.blurb: The west side's cultural engine — Hongdae, Yeonnam, Hapjeong, Mangwon. Indie music, thrift, cafes and nightlife that never fully stops. Two neighbourhoods here get their own zone: Hongdae and Mangwon.

seongdong.blurb: Riverside east Seoul, and the address everyone means when they say Seongsu. One neighbourhood here gets its own zone: Seongsu-dong.

dongdaemun.blurb: East of the old gate — wholesale fashion markets and the sprawling Gyeongdong medicinal-herb market. Working, unpolished, real.

jungnang.blurb: North-eastern residential district under the Achasan ridge. Quiet, green, off the tourist map.

gwangjin.blurb: Riverside east Seoul around Konkuk University — a dense student drinking quarter with a Chinese-Korean community and a lamb-skewer alley (양꼬치 거리) of self-rotating charcoal skewers, best after dark, plus Children's Grand Park and the Ttukseom waterfront. Not one of the video-covered neighbourhoods, so no zone here yet — flag it if that changes.

gangbuk.blurb: Northern residential district at the foot of Bukhansan — trailheads, apartment blocks, everyday markets.

nowon.blurb: Far north-east, dense residential 'bed town' — universities, family blocks, bathhouses.

dobong.blurb: Seoul's northern tip against Dobongsan — almost entirely residential, mountain-ringed, breathable.

seongbuk.blurb: 'North of the fortress' — hillside embassies and old money, a cluster of small museums, and the Hanyang city-wall trail over the ridge into Bukchon. The wall walk past Naksan Park is lit and open around the clock.

yeongdeungpo.blurb: South-bank finance district — the National Assembly, IFC, The Hyundai Seoul, Korea's largest Chinatown in Daerim — plus Mullae-dong, an old-town-grit pocket that doesn't feel duplicative of anywhere else in Seoul. One neighbourhood here gets its own zone: Mullae-dong.

dongjak.blurb: South-central, residential and green — Boramae Park, the Noryangjin fish market and exam-cram district, the national cemetery.

yangcheon.blurb: South-western residential district — Mokdong's towers and its famous wall of after-school academies. Home to the Seoul Immigration Office.

gwanak.blurb: Southern district built around Seoul National University and Nakseongdae — student-priced food, hillside lanes, Gwanaksan hiking.

guro.blurb: South-west — old textile mills reborn as 'G Valley', a startup and IT cluster, plus a large multicultural quarter.

geumcheon.blurb: Seoul's southern edge — industrial parks, outlet malls, and late-night pojangmacha tents.

gangseo.blurb: Far west around Gimpo Airport — Korea's first airport and the Magok tech development, plus Banghwa wetlands.
also: Gimpo Airport — domestic Jeju flights leave from here

songpa.blurb: South-east — Lotte World Tower, Seokchon Lake, Olympic Park. Big, new, family-oriented behind the towers.

gangdong.blurb: Seoul's south-eastern corner on the Han River — the Amsa prehistoric site, riverside parks, and a glass-floored bridge observatory.

gangnam.blurb: The wealthy south — corporate towers, hagwon, clinics, COEX. Skip Gangnam Station; the walkable part is the Sinsa–Garosu-gil–Dosan–Apgujeong spine of concept retail and cafes. A second video source independently lands on the same call: 'don't go out of your way... don't cross the water if you have 4 days.' One neighbourhood here gets its own zone: Sinsa–Apgujeong.

seocho.blurb: West of Gangnam — the courthouse district, Seoul Arts Center, and Banpo's Moonlight Rainbow Fountain arcing off the bridge.

ikseondong.name: Ikseon-dong
ikseondong.blurb: A tight grid of 1920s 'urban hanok' just south of Jongno 3-ga — alleys barely wide enough for two, filled with cafes, dessert bars and small restaurants. Not a preserved showpiece like Bukchon; a lived-in warren you wander into and get lost in. Busiest evenings and weekends. One travel couple's pick for 'one night in Seoul, want the quintessential experience': walk it and eat at the K-BBQ quadrant — a whole section of the alleys is outdoor Korean BBQ, packed year-round even in a snowstorm. Also here: a saltbread bakery branch, and a cafe that looks ordinary at street level but opens into four floors of curated mid-century furniture.

bukchon.name: Bukchon + Gyeongbokgung
bukchon.blurb: Bukchon Hanok Village and Gyeongbokgung Palace, right next to each other — 'a perfect first day,' 'a perfect sandwich of sightseeing.' People reportedly still live in the hanoks; stay on the public lanes and keep it quiet. Real, enforced restrictions apply on one street (Bukchon-ro 11-gil, no visits 5pm–10am, ₩100,000 fine) plus a chartered-bus ban citywide — none of that blocks a normal daytime walk-through. Best before 8am or after 5pm to skip the crowds. Jura Optique (vintage sunglasses) and Cafe Onion sit in the commerce area just off the hanok alleys. Even after a year of full-time travel and dozens of palaces, one couple called Gyeongbokgung a genuine jaw-dropper — don't let palace fatigue talk you out of it.

myeongdong.name: Myeongdong
myeongdong.blurb: Dead-centre Seoul and the city's shopping engine — global and Korean brands, department stores, a dense run of K-beauty flagships, budget racks and luxury a block apart. A pedestrian core by day; a street-food night market after dark. Two independent travel-video sources land on the same verdict: 'the Times Square of Seoul' — worth a short walk-through (graze the night market, don't plan a real dinner around it), but actively avoid using it as a base. Worst traffic and cab access in the city if you stay here; roughly three-quarters of the crowd on the ground is non-Korean tourists.

euljiro.name: Euljiro
euljiro.blurb: Old tool, lighting and print wholesale district — since ~2016, a dense layer of design bars and cafes hidden on unmarked upper floors of decaying buildings, the aesthetic opposite of Gangnam. One couple's framing: 'paper factories by day, insane eateries and bars by night' — neon-heavy, Blade-Runner-at-night, right off central Myeongdong; don't bother in daytime. Being cleared block by block through 2030 — go while it's there. Pick: Purr, a space-age themed wine bar, with a K-BBQ spot doing the classics plus unusual sides just down the block. ~15 min on foot to Jongno 3-ga and Gwangjang Market.

itaewon.name: Itaewon
itaewon.blurb: Seoul's most international quarter, grown up serving the old US base — global food, nightlife, and Itaewon Antique Furniture Street (~1.4 km, ~2,400 shops, a vintage festival every May and October). Also the site of the 2022 Halloween crowd-crush; a memorial alley is signposted off the main strip. One couple's hot take: go for sleepy daytime Itaewon — coffee, a wander through windy hilly back streets, a wine bar in the evening — rather than just the nightlife. Much of the centre is mid-redevelopment.

haebangchon.name: Haebangchon (HBC)
haebangchon.blurb: A travel couple's outright #1 stay pick in all of Seoul: the most diverse neighborhood in the city, hilly enough for surprise skyline views round every corner, a trendy-but-mature vibe (25–35s, not teenage energy). No metro in the neighborhood itself — budget a ~15-min cab to anywhere. Haebangchon Market is a covered alley of small restaurants, an 'Instagrammy town square.' Walking distance to Itaewon and to Leeum in Hannam-dong.

hannam.name: Hannam-dong
hannam.blurb: Probably the trendiest neighborhood in Seoul — cute Korean trendy brands, boutique flagships of stores that have satellite locations elsewhere, hilly and pretty. Best in the evening into dinner. One couple's favorite Italian restaurant in all of Seoul (Atta) and what may be the best tiramisu either of them has had (Lillian) are both here. Leeum Museum of Art anchors the neighborhood by day. Their framing: 'Itaewon for nights, Hannam for days.'

hongdae.name: Hongdae
hongdae.blurb: The arts-and-party district around Hongik University. The east side is loud and commercial; the west side, past Yanghwa-ro and north of Jandari-ro, is calmer and thick with independent cafes. Saturday brings the Free Market on the playground (noon–6, Mar–Nov). A second video source independently downgrades the main drag — near-duplicate of Myeongdong, 'too famous to skip, but you'll go and not be that impressed' — and agrees Yeonnam-dong next door, underrated and quieter with wine bars, is the better use of the same walk.

mangwon.name: Mangwon
mangwon.blurb: A travel couple's #2 stay pick in all of Seoul, right behind Haebangchon — called it the 'platonic ideal' of a Seoul neighborhood. Good traditional Korean food at Mangwon Market plus global restaurants; part of / near the greater Hongdae area. 'I would consider myself very lucky to stay here if I went back to Seoul.'

seongsu.name: Seongsu-dong
seongsu.blurb: Seoul's converted-warehouse district — concept stores, flagship pop-ups (Yeonmujang-gil, west and east, from Seongsu Stn Exits 3/4), and the densest run of design cafes in the city. Pop-ups open ~11am–noon, go in the afternoon; weekday beats weekend queues. A second video source corroborates the pattern independently: main drag = 'literally Bedford Ave, Williamsburg,' packed and commercial — wander a couple of side streets and it turns residential, real locals, better food and shops. Their comparison: Seongsu wins on vintage shopping, Hannam-dong wins on food and bars.

mullae.name: Mullae-dong
mullae.blurb: An old steel-workshop and warehouse district turned artist studios, cafes and small music venues — working metalworkers still share the streets with the galleries. 'Bushwick vibes,' genuinely gritty rather than styled that way. Skip it on a first, 4-day trip; worth it on a longer stay or a repeat visit, especially at night. Zero foreigners seen on one visit; skews late-20s/30s local. Called 'maybe unrivaled' old-town grit among Seoul neighborhoods that otherwise start to blur together — 'by next year this is going to be on everybody's radar.'

sinsa.name: Sinsa–Apgujeong
sinsa.blurb: Not Gangnam Station — that's a transit hub. The part to walk is the Line 3 spine: Sinsa, Garosu-gil and its quieter parallel Serosu-gil, Dosan Park, Apgujeong Rodeo, Cheongdam — flagship concept stores, galleries, and expensive coffee. The Sinbundang Line drops you straight in from Bundang.

places.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
places.note: Starts at Cheonggye Plaza by Gwanghwamun and runs about 11 km east. Walk it, put your feet in, watch for the koi. Possible match for a second video source's 'skip' stream — visited in peak summer heat and called 'literally nothing.' Not confirmed as the same stream.

places.name: Arario Museum in Space
places.note: Set in Kim Swoo-geun's 1971 SPACE building beside Changdeokgung — the architecture is the reason to come.

places.name: Cheongsudang
places.note: A Japanese-garden teahouse in the Ikseon-dong hanok alleys. Expect a wait at peak hours.

places.name: Naksan Park
places.note: Hanyang City Wall trail, lit at night, full city panorama. Runs the Jongno/Seongbuk border.

places.name: Changdeokgung Palace
places.note: The most intact Joseon palace, laid out to follow the hills rather than a grid. The Huwon 'Secret Garden' is a separate timed guided tour — book ahead.

places.name: Ssamziegil
places.note: A ramp of ~70 small craft/design studios spiralling around an open courtyard, off Insadong's main street.

places.name: Jogyesa Temple
places.note: Head temple of the Jogye order, a block off Insadong.

places.name: Ikseon Banjoo
places.note: Korean small plates with a drink alongside, in the Ikseon-dong hanok alleys.

places.name: Rain Report

places.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
places.note: Pair with Bukchon as a first day. A genuine highlight even for the palace-fatigued.

places.name: Jura Optique
places.note: Vintage sunglasses shop — confirmed via Naver to be in Seongsu-dong (Seongdong-gu), not the Bukchon commerce street as originally assumed. Good deals.

places.name: Cafe Onion — Bukchon
places.note: The well-known industrial-bakery cafe chain's Bukchon branch.

places.name: Gwangjang Market
places.note: Flagged skip by a second video source ('most touristy market in Seoul') — still worth a quick stop for bindaetteok and yukhoe. The 2F vintage-clothing floor is the part most people miss.

places.name: Dongmyo Flea Market
places.note: The serious thrift dig — ₩1,000 piles of clothes, plus old cameras, LPs and radios. Come 10am Sat/Sun for the freshest piles.

places.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
places.note: Zaha Hadid, 2014. The LED-rose field lights up after dark.

places.name: Myeongdong Night Market
places.note: Evening street-food carts. Tourist-priced — graze, don't count on it for dinner.

places.name: Namdaemun Market
places.note: Korea's biggest traditional market. The galchi-jorim and oyster-soup alleys are the meal.

places.name: Olive Young — Myeongdong Town
places.note: The flagship K-beauty store; branches sit on nearly every block elsewhere.

places.name: Vands Clinic — Myeongdong
places.hours: By appointment — clinic open Mon–Fri 09:30–21:00, Sat/Sun 09:30–18:00
places.note: Skin/derma clinic — confirm exact name and book ahead for a treatment.

places.name: Jaemiro Cartoon Street
places.note: An open-air webtoon-and-cartoon street climbing from Myeongdong toward Namsan.

places.name: Per
places.note: Space-age-themed wine bar in Euljiro — 'one of the cutest little wine bars I've ever been to.'

places.name: Backdon
places.note: K-BBQ spot a short walk from Per — 'all the classics plus some crazy sides.'

places.name: Hwanghak-dong Flea Market
places.note: ~1,000 stalls across five alleys of machinery, vinyl, vintage cameras and old electronics. No clothing here — Dongmyo is close by for that.

places.name: National Museum of Korea
places.note: Free general admission and enormous — give it half a day. Don't miss the Room of Quiet Contemplation.

places.name: Leeum Museum of Art
places.note: Three buildings by Botta, Nouvel and Koolhaas — the architecture is half the visit. Reserve timed entry.

places.name: Fountain, Itaewon
places.note: Bar/club in Itaewon — verify it's still open before building a night around it.

places.name: Hills and Europa
places.note: A jazz bar and cafe in the Itaewon–Hannam belt.

places.name: Franc
places.hours: Evenings from ~16:00 (check Naver for closing time)
places.note: A French-style restaurant — confirmed via Naver to be on Sinheung-ro in Haebangchon (near Noksapyeong Station), not core Itaewon as originally assumed.

places.name: Barou
places.note: Bohemian-vibe wine bar in Itaewon — a glass of wine and pasta.

places.name: Sunset-cocktail bar — Itaewon
places.note: Near a spot 'where everybody watches sunset.' Unnamed in the source video — pinned to a bar called "Sunset Beach" on this stretch of Itaewon-ro as the closest Google Maps match; confirm this is the right spot.

places.name: Itaewon Antique Furniture Street
places.note: ~1.4km, ~2,400 shops. The Antique & Vintage Festival runs every May and October — October lands inside the trip window.

places.name: Haebangchon Market
places.note: A covered, winding alley of small restaurants — 'an Instagrammy town square.'

places.name: Jamsugyo-jip
places.note: Samgyeopsal pick in Haebangchon — very thinly sliced pork.

places.note: The Hannam-dong cafe with 'the best tiramisu I may have ever had.'

places.name: Cactus Curry Club

places.name: Taqueria El Domingo
places.note: Called 'the best tacos in the city.' Confirmed via Google Maps to be in Mangwon-dong, Mapo-gu — not the Itaewon/HBC belt as originally guessed.

places.name: Jingwansa
places.note: An active temple — keep your voice to a whisper. The teahouse on the grounds does ssanghwacha and red-bean patjuk.

places.name: Hongjecheon Waterfall
places.note: Cafe Popo sits right beside it — its proceeds fund student scholarships.

places.name: Sosin Isso
places.note: Braised short rib and glass noodles in a spicy rosé sauce.

places.name: Mangwon Market
places.note: Traditional market with good Korean food plus global restaurants around it.

places.name: Seoul Forest
places.note: Best early morning — deer paddock, wetland boardwalk, a lake that goes full Monet.

places.name: Haus Nowhere Seongsu
places.note: Gentle Monster's Seongsu concept space — rotating room-scale installations.

places.name: Maison Margiela Cafe
places.note: Confirmed via Google Maps: this is the Maison Margiela flagship café in Hannam-dong (Yongsan), not Seongsu — moved from the seongdong district.

places.name: Point of View
places.note: Stationery treated as art objects.

places.name: Cafe Stakke
places.note: A Danish-style cafe — favorite spot on Seongsu's crowded main drag.

places.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
places.note: Quieter riverside than Yeouido — bike paths, a summer pool.

places.name: Gyeongdong Market
places.note: A medicinal-herb market that now sells everything. Andongjip is inside.

places.name: Seoul Folk Flea Market
places.note: 885 shops, mostly indoors, colour-zoned. A 10-minute walk from Dongmyo.

places.name: Konkuk University area
places.note: Lamb-skewer alley plus Yanbian beer; the Common Ground container mall is a short walk.

places.name: Minaribat Orisanyang
places.note: Mullae-dong duck BBQ — 'phenomenal, if you like duck, you got to go.'

places.name: Haebangeum
places.note: Listening bar right after the duck BBQ — 'perfect little date-night vibe.'

places.name: Boramae Park
places.note: An old air-force field with planes on display. Haechi House inside sells 'Seoul Playbook 365.'

places.name: Noryangjin Fish Market
places.note: Buy fish downstairs, carry it up to a restaurant that cooks it. Bring a family member — it can get pushy.

places.name: Seoul Botanic Park
places.note: A wetland park built around a domed glasshouse of tropical and Mediterranean plants.

places.name: Garosu-gil / Serosu-gil
places.note: Tree-lined concept retail; the parallel back-alley Serosu-gil is where the energy moved.

places.name: Haus Dosan
places.note: Gentle Monster + Tamburins + Nudake at Dosan Park. Pick this OR Haus Nowhere in Seongsu — not both.

places.name: Gangnam vintage
places.note: Curated resale — a pricier tier than a Dongmyo dig.

places.name: Starfield Library (COEX)
places.note: The famous one — the branch Jake said to skip. Decide before adding to a day.

places.name: Bongeunsa
places.note: Across the road from COEX — a calmer temple option if Jingwansa slips.

places.name: Banpo Moonlight Rainbow Fountain
places.note: Watch from Banpo Hangang Park with fried chicken on your lap — Hyodo Chicken is the premium pick nearby.

places.name: Root Hongdae
places.note: Used-apparel/vintage store on Yanghwa-ro (basement level), ~180m from Hongik Univ. Station Exit 9. Fits the Hongdae thrift tier already flagged in the itinerary (Y2K/streetwear/Americana, ₩15–80k, best Fri/Sat evening).

places.name: SOLD OUT (Dongmyo vintage)
places.note: Used-apparel/vintage stall in the Dongmyo Flea Market cluster, ~257m from Dongmyo Station Exit 3 (address: 235-1 Sungin-dong). Not findable on Google Maps — coordinates interpolated between Dongmyo Station and the existing Dongmyo/Hwanghak pins, not a confirmed on-the-ground pin.

places.name: MUSINSA Empty Seongsu
places.note: MUSINSA's flagship concept/gallery store in a striking glass-and-black-box building on Seongsui-ro — exactly the 'concept retail' taste match Seongsu keeps coming up for. Rotating installations/exhibits, not just a shop floor.

places.name: Coor
places.note: Minimalist fashion boutique on Yeonmujang-gil — the same pop-up spine Seongsu's whole scene is built around, between Ttukseom and Seongsu stations.

places.name: Tom Greyhound Seongsu
places.note: Multi-brand concept store, Yeonmujang-gil — striking cross-pattern facade. Same street as Coor; a natural pairing on a Seongsu pop-up afternoon.

places.name: Omnipeople
places.note: Used-apparel/vintage store ('Omnipeople · Heavy'), ~410m from Hongik Univ. Station Exit 7. Fits the Hongdae thrift tier alongside Root Hongdae. Address confirmed 2026-09-14 against Jake's own Google Maps listing (348-48 Seogyo-dong matches) — the 335-35 on the KakaoMap screenshot was a different address string, not a wrong pin.

places.name: Wooyoungmi Itaewon Flagship
places.note: Architectural flagship (curved glass-block facade, poured-concrete interior with a rooftop cafe) for the Korean menswear label — a design/concept-retail stop inside the Itaewon walk.

places.name: Juun.J Dosan Flagship Store
places.note: Menswear flagship near Apgujeong Rodeo — pairs with the Sinsa/Dosan Park/Garosu-gil spine. The building itself is the draw: a stark black angular pyramid-roofed volume.

places.name: Seoul Hall of Urbanism & Architecture
places.hours: 10:00–19:00, free admission — closed for Chuseok 9/25 & National Holiday 10/5
places.note: Free exhibit hall right by City Hall/Gwanghwamun — scale models of Seoul, urban-planning and architecture exhibits. A quick, no-cost add to a Cluster B (downtown) day.

places.name: Cafe Saeraul
places.note: Resolves the long-standing '❓ Saeraul' unknown from the itinerary master list — a hanok-courtyard cafe in Yeonhui-dong, second building on the lot, with a striking bamboo/stone/water courtyard lit at night. Cafe + dessert + cocktails (the reviews-tab drink shown was clearly alcoholic).

places.name: Olympic Park
places.note: Huge, free, outdoor — 1988 Olympics venue turned sculpture park + Seoul Olympic Museum. Grandma's home base is walking/short-transit distance from here (Songpa, near Olympic Park). Good jet-lag-recovery day: minimal transit, minimal decision fatigue.

places.name: Seokchon Lake
places.note: Walking loop around a lake right by Lotte World Tower — pleasant any time, lit up at night. A low-effort closer near home, especially in the evening.

places.name: Lotte World Tower & Seoul Sky
places.hours: Seoul Sky observation deck ~10:30–22:00 daily (check for seasonal hours)
places.note: Korea's tallest building — observation deck (Seoul Sky), mall, and Lotte World theme park next door if there's appetite for it. One subway stop or a walk from Olympic Park / grandma's, depending on exact address. A low-effort evening closer.

places.name: Songni-dan-gil
places.note: Songpa's own cafe-and-restaurant strip (the area's answer to Gyeongridan-gil/Yeonnam-dong-style redevelopment), a short walk from Seokchon Lake. Good low-key option on a day anchored near home. ⚠️ Pin resolved to a shop tagged with this street name, not a precise street centerline — treat as approximate.

places.name: Mibbedong
places.note: Salmon noodle spot, on Jake's own pick list. Near the Yeonnam-dong/Hongdae edge (Donggyo-ro).

places.note: Vintage/thrift shop priced by weight (~₩1,990-2,390/100g; over 5kg gets a free scarf). 42-24 Hwayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu -- 551m from Konkuk Univ. Station Exit 1. Confirmed correct via Naver Map (2026-09-15): Gwangjin-gu was right, not Seongsu as originally described.

places.note: Fashion accessories shop in Seongsu, on Jake's pick list.

places.name: The Hyundai Seoul
places.note: Yeouido's flagship department store/mall, famous for its huge indoor atrium (real trees, a waterfall, a skylight ceiling) and a ground-floor Louis Vuitton anchor. On Jake's pick list.

places.name: Musinsa Empty Apgujeong
places.note: Musinsa's Apgujeong concept store (basement level, Eonju-ro), distinct from the existing Seongsu branch (musinsaempty).

places.name: Obscura
places.note: Small gallery/studio space, on Jake's pick list as an Apgujeong spot. ⚠️ Geocoded to a single-story converted building on Seongbuk-ro 23-gil, Seongbuk-gu -- not Apgujeong/Gangnam-gu. The name matched exactly but the neighborhood didn't; confirm on Naver whether this is the right branch/location before routing a day around it.

places.name: London Bagel Museum — Anguk
places.hours: Check on Naver (long lines, arrive early)
places.note: Seoul's famously-queued bagel shop, original Anguk/Bukchon branch (20 Bukchon-ro 4-gil) -- huge case of flavored bagels, cream cheeses and sandwiches. On Jake's pick list.

places.name: Geumgeum
places.note: Seongsu-dong restaurant known for perilla-oil noodles topped with a raw egg yolk, alongside char siu-style pork. On Jake's pick list.

places.name: Hyodo Chicken
places.note: Premium fried chicken from the team behind two-Michelin-star Mingles -- gochujang-glaze and other avant-garde flavors. Previously flagged in the research corpus as a Banpo Fountain pairing (order and bring to the show), not a Banpo-area storefront. ⚠️ Only findable branch (Janghanpyeong, Dongdaemun-gu) is well away from Banpo/Seocho-gu -- likely delivery-focused rather than a destination storefront; confirm before routing a day around it.

places.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
places.note: Famous knife-cut noodle (kalguksu) and mandu institution just off Myeongdong's main strip -- a Seoul classic. On Jake's pick list.

places.name: Chicken In The Kitchen
places.note: Fried chicken spot near Yeonnam-dong/Hongdae (Wausan-ro). On Jake's pick list. ⚠️ A second branch exists near Gyeongbokgung/Jahamun-ro (Jongno-gu) -- this pin is the Mapo-gu one; confirm which was meant.

places.name: Break Silence
places.note: A highly popular, low-key loft-style music bar and vintage concept shop in Seongsu-dong -- cozy, hidden hangout spinning everything from hip-hop and indie to electronic. Beyond cocktails and vinyl, there's a retail section for browsing vintage streetwear and, on Sundays, custom silk-screen T-shirt printing. 👉 Go on a Sunday -- that's when they have DJs.
